title: Transient mixed-serve during rollback due to routing transaction ordering bug
creator: Aisha Patel
description: During a routine canary-to-production rollout on 2026-03-09 we observed a transient window where traffic was split across two incompatible model variants despite a triggered rollback. This led to increased 5xx errors for a subset of tenant routes and inconsistent inference results for customers pinned to a single version. Investigation showed the rollout controller applied route translation changes and version pin-state updates out of order under load, producing a short-lived mixed-serve state while caches and sidecars reconciled.
timeline: 2026-03-09T03:56Z - Monitoring: spike in 5xxs on route /chat for 3 tenants; alert routed to on-call
2026-03-09T04:01Z - On-call triage: rollback initiated via console (route pin-state requested to previous model)
2026-03-09T04:03Z - Partial rollback visible in control plane, some worker sidecars still serving new variant (mixed-serve)
2026-03-09T04:10Z - Mitigation: manual route pin and enforced node drain for canary workers; traffic stabilized by 04:18Z
2026-03-09T05:00Z - Post-incident: incident declared, ticket opened, and initial notes captured
2026-03-11T10:12Z - Repro harness run locally with concurrent route+pin updates reproduced mixed-serve reliably
2026-03-12T15:30Z - Code fix attempt: add ordering guarantees in rollout controller; peer review opened
2026-03-13T09:00Z - Integration tests added for atomic route/pin update; design doc for stronger reconciliation published
impact: Approximately 0.6% of API requests to the affected routes returned mismatched outputs or 5xx errors during the 15-minute window. Two paying customers reported degraded inference quality and one internal SLA alert for increased error budget burn occurred. No data exfiltration or security breach observed.
detection: Automated SLO-based alerting (routes:5xx-rate) flagged the spike. On-call noticed divergence in the Console per-route model version graph and customer escalation corroborated the issue.
root_cause: Race condition in the rollout controller: non-atomic update sequence where route translation (routing table) changes were committed and published before the version pin-state write completed. Worker sidecars consume routing updates and may accept requests for the newly announced model variant before their local pin-state cache is refreshed. Under moderate concurrency this produced transient dual-serving across the fleet.
immediate_remediation: Manually applied a force-pin for affected routes to the stable model version (console action)
Drained and restarted canary worker pods to purge stale pin caches
Increased verbosity on rollout controller logs and enabled debug tracing for route publish paths
Temporarily reduced parallelism on promotions to limit simultaneous routing updates
permanent_fixes: Make route translation + pin-state update atomic in controller: wrap both writes in a single DB transaction and publish a single reconciled event
Introduce a short, configurable quiesce period between routing publication and worker accept window to allow caches to reconverge
Add pre-promotion integration test in CI that runs a full canary->promote->rollback cycle under synthetic concurrent traffic and asserts no mixed-serve occurs
Enhance sidecar to reject requests if its pin-state version is older than the routing table version (fail-fast) and trigger a reconcile
Record route/pin version headers on responses for easier post-incident tracing
